def plot_solution(
    model,
    pde,
    num_points: int = 1000,
    save_path: str | None = None,
    return_figs: bool = False,
    time_point: float | None = None,
):  # pragma: no cover
    """Exact and predicted solution as two interactive 3-D surfaces.

    Args:
        model: The trained PINN model.
        pde: The PDE instance.
        num_points: Total grid points (``sqrt(num_points)`` per axis, and as many
            time frames for an animated 2-D plot).
        save_path: Optional ``.html`` path; writes ``*_exact.html`` and ``*_predicted.html``.
        return_figs: Return ``(exact_fig, predicted_fig)`` instead of saving/showing.
        time_point: Time of the slice for 2-D PDEs (animated over time when
            omitted). 1-D PDEs always show the whole ``(x, t)`` surface: a
            single-time slice of a 1-D field is a line, which a surface cannot draw.
    """
    n = int(np.sqrt(num_points))
    if pde.dimension == 2:
        times = (
            [float(time_point)]
            if time_point is not None
            else list(np.linspace(float(pde.time_domain[0]), float(pde.time_domain[1]), n))
        )
        grids = [solution_grid(model, pde, n, t) for t in times]
        A, B = grids[0][0], grids[0][1]
        preds = [g[2] for g in grids]
        exacts = [g[3] for g in grids]
    else:
        A, B, pred, exact = solution_grid(model, pde, n)
        times, preds, exacts = [None], [pred], [exact]

    if exacts[0] is None:
        exact_fig = go.Figure()
        exacts = [None] * len(exacts)
    else:
        exact_fig = go.Figure(
            data=[go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=exacts[0], colorscale="viridis", showscale=False)]
        )
    predicted_fig = go.Figure(
        data=[go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=preds[0], colorscale="plasma", showscale=False)]
    )
    if len(times) > 1:
        labels = [f"t={t:.2f}" for t in times]
        if exacts[0] is not None:
            exact_fig.frames = [
                go.Frame(data=[go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=z)], name=label)
                for z, label in zip(exacts, labels, strict=False)
            ]
        predicted_fig.frames = [
            go.Frame(data=[go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=z)], name=label)
            for z, label in zip(preds, labels, strict=False)
        ]
        sliders = [
            dict(
                steps=[dict(method="animate", args=[[label]], label=label) for label in labels],
                currentvalue=dict(visible=True, prefix="Time: "),
                len=0.9,
            )
        ]
        exact_fig.update_layout(sliders=sliders)
        predicted_fig.update_layout(sliders=sliders)

    axis = dict(
        showgrid=True,
        zeroline=True,
        showline=True,
        showticklabels=True,
        showspikes=False,
        showbackground=True,
        backgroundcolor="rgba(240, 240, 240, 0.5)",
    )
    scene = dict(
        xaxis=dict(title="x", **axis),
        yaxis=dict(title="t" if pde.dimension == 1 else "y", **axis),
        zaxis=dict(title="u(x,t)" if pde.dimension == 1 else "u(x,y,t)", **axis),
        camera=dict(
            up=dict(x=0, y=0, z=1), center=dict(x=0, y=0, z=0), eye=dict(x=1.5, y=1.5, z=1.5)
        ),
        dragmode="turntable",
        aspectmode="cube",
    )
    margin = dict(l=0, r=0, b=0, t=30)
    exact_title = "Exact Solution" if exacts[0] is not None else "No exact solution configured"
    exact_fig.update_layout(title=exact_title, scene=scene, margin=margin)
    predicted_fig.update_layout(title="PINN Prediction", scene=scene, margin=margin)

    if return_figs:
        return exact_fig, predicted_fig
    if save_path:
        exact_fig.write_html(save_path.replace(".html", "_exact.html"))
        predicted_fig.write_html(save_path.replace(".html", "_predicted.html"))
    else:
        exact_fig.show()
        predicted_fig.show()

def solution_grid(
    model, pde, n: int, t: float | None = None
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Evaluate ``model`` and ``pde.exact_solution`` on a regular grid.

    1-D PDEs use an ``(x, t)`` grid over the whole time domain, or the single
    time ``t`` when given. 2-D PDEs use an ``(x1, x2)`` grid at time ``t``
    (default: the start of the time domain).

    Args:
        model: Trained network; its parameters' device is used.
        pde: PDE providing the domain and ``exact_solution``.
        n: Points per axis.
        t: Optional time of the slice.

    Returns:
        ``(A, B, u_pred, u_exact)``, each of shape ``(n, n)`` (or ``(n, 1)``
        for a single-time 1-D slice), with ``A, B`` the grid coordinates and
        ``u_pred`` the model's output channel 0. ``u_exact`` is ``None`` when
        the PDE has no exact solution.
    """
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    t_lo, t_hi = float(pde.time_domain[0]), float(pde.time_domain[1])
    if pde.dimension == 1:
        a = torch.linspace(pde.domain[0][0], pde.domain[0][1], n, device=device)
        b = (
            torch.tensor([float(t)], device=device)
            if t is not None
            else torch.linspace(t_lo, t_hi, n, device=device)
        )
        A, B = torch.meshgrid(a, b, indexing="ij")
        x = A.reshape(-1, 1)
        tt = B.reshape(-1, 1)
    else:
        a = torch.linspace(pde.domain[0][0], pde.domain[0][1], n, device=device)
        b = torch.linspace(pde.domain[1][0], pde.domain[1][1], n, device=device)
        A, B = torch.meshgrid(a, b, indexing="ij")
        x = torch.stack([A.reshape(-1), B.reshape(-1)], dim=1)
        tt = torch.full((x.shape[0], 1), t_lo if t is None else float(t), device=device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        u_pred = model(torch.cat([x, tt], dim=1))[:, 0:1]
        u_exact = pde.exact_solution(x, tt)
    shape = A.shape
    return (
        A.cpu().numpy(),
        B.cpu().numpy(),
        u_pred.reshape(shape).cpu().numpy(),
        None if u_exact is None else u_exact.reshape(shape).cpu().numpy(),
    )

def plot_training_history(trainer, save_path=None):  # pragma: no cover
    """Loss curves on a log axis, plus loss-weight curves when adaptive weights are on.

    Only the ``*_loss`` series are drawn: ``val_loss`` at the epochs it was
    measured, the others once per epoch. The learning rate and parameter
    trajectories are not losses and are left out.
    """
    history = trainer.history
    epochs, val_epochs = loss_curve_epochs(history, trainer.validation_frequency)
    loss_keys = [key for key, values in history.items() if key.endswith("_loss") and values]
    weights = np.array(history.get("loss_weights", []))
    with_weights = trainer.use_adaptive_weights and len(weights) > 0
    if with_weights:
        fig = make_subplots(rows=2, cols=1, subplot_titles=("Losses", "Loss Weights"))
    else:
        fig = go.Figure()
    loss_cell = {"row": 1, "col": 1} if with_weights else {}
    for key in loss_keys:
        x = val_epochs if key == "val_loss" else epochs[: len(history[key])]
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=x, y=history[key], name=key, mode="lines"), **loss_cell)
    if with_weights:
        for i, component in enumerate(["residual", "boundary", "initial"]):
            if i < weights.shape[1]:
                fig.add_trace(
                    go.Scatter(
                        x=epochs[: len(weights)],
                        y=weights[:, i],
                        name=f"{component}_weight",
                        mode="lines",
                    ),
                    row=2,
                    col=1,
                )
        fig.update_layout(title="Training History", height=800)
        fig.update_yaxes(type="log", title="Loss", row=1, col=1)
        fig.update_yaxes(title="Weight Value", row=2, col=1)
        fig.update_xaxes(title="Epoch", row=2, col=1)
    else:
        fig.update_layout(
            title="Training History", xaxis_title="Epoch", yaxis_title="Loss", yaxis_type="log"
        )
    if save_path:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(save_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        _write_plotly(fig, save_path)

def plot_solution_comparison(trainer, num_points=50, save_path=None):  # pragma: no cover
    """Exact, predicted and log-error surfaces side by side.

    ``num_points`` is the grid size per axis. 2-D PDEs get ten time frames
    with a slider and a Play button. Skipped when the PDE has no exact solution.
    """
    pde, model = trainer.pde, trainer.model
    if not pde.has_exact_solution:
        _LOGGER.info("No exact solution configured; skipping the solution comparison plot")
        return
    titles = ("Exact", "PINN Predicted", "Log Min Error")
    specs = [[{"type": "surface"}] * 3]
    if pde.dimension == 2:
        times = np.linspace(float(pde.time_domain[0]), float(pde.time_domain[1]), 10)
        frames = []
        for t in times:
            A, B, pred, exact = solution_grid(model, pde, num_points, t)
            frames.append(
                go.Frame(
                    data=[
                        go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=exact, colorscale="viridis", showscale=False),
                        go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=pred, colorscale="viridis", showscale=False),
                        go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=_log_min_error(pred, exact), colorscale="viridis"),
                    ],
                    traces=[0, 1, 2],
                    name=f"t={t:.2f}",
                )
            )
        fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=3, subplot_titles=titles, specs=specs)
        for col, trace in enumerate(frames[0].data, start=1):
            fig.add_trace(trace, row=1, col=col)
        fig.frames = frames
        fig.update_layout(
            title="Solution Comparison (2D)",
            width=1800,
            height=600,
            updatemenus=[
                {
                    "type": "buttons",
                    "showactive": False,
                    "buttons": [
                        {
                            "label": "Play",
                            "method": "animate",
                            "args": [
                                None,
                                {"frame": {"duration": 500, "redraw": True}, "fromcurrent": True},
                            ],
                        }
                    ],
                }
            ],
            sliders=[
                {
                    "currentvalue": {"prefix": "t="},
                    "steps": [
                        {
                            "args": [
                                [f.name],
                                {"frame": {"duration": 0, "redraw": True}, "mode": "immediate"},
                            ],
                            "label": f.name,
                            "method": "animate",
                        }
                        for f in frames
                    ],
                }
            ],
        )
    else:
        A, B, pred, exact = solution_grid(model, pde, num_points)
        fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=3, subplot_titles=titles, specs=specs)
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Surface(x=A, y=B, z=exact, colorscale="viridis", showscale=False), row=1, col=1
        )
        fig.add_trace(

                x=A,

        )
        axes = dict(xaxis_title="x", yaxis_title="t", zaxis_title="u(x,t)")
        fig.update_layout(

            height=600,
            scene=axes,
            scene2=axes,
            scene3=axes,
        )

        _write_plotly(fig, save_path)

def plot_collocation_evolution(trainer, save_path=None):  # pragma: no cover
    """2×2 grid: point snapshots over training, and initial/mid/final densities.

    1-D PDEs are drawn in the ``(x, t)`` plane, 2-D PDEs in the ``(x, y)`` plane.
    """
    history = getattr(trainer, "points_history", None)
    if not history:
        _LOGGER.warning("No collocation points history available")
        return
    pde = trainer.pde
    if pde.dimension == 1:
        x_range, y_range, ylabel = pde.domain[0], pde.time_domain, "t"
        progression_title = "Progression of Points"
    else:
        x_range, y_range, ylabel = pde.domain[0], pde.domain[1], "y"
        progression_title = "Progression of Points (x-y projection)"

    fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 14))
    fig.suptitle("Evolution of Collocation Points", fontsize=20)

    ax = axs[0, 0]
    for idx in _snapshot_indices(len(history)):
        points = history[idx]
        ax.scatter(
            points[:, 0],
            points[:, 1],
            s=3,
            alpha=0.5,
            label=f"Snapshot {idx}",
            marker=".",
            edgecolors="none",
        )
    ax.set_title(progression_title, fontsize=16)
    ax.legend(fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("x", fontsize=14)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=14)
    ax.set_xlim(x_range)
    ax.set_ylim(y_range)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    mid = len(history) // 2
    for ax, points, cmap, title in [
        (axs[0, 1], history[0], plt.cm.Blues, "Initial Distribution"),
        (axs[1, 0], history[mid], plt.cm.Greens, f"Intermediate Distribution (Snapshot {mid})"),
        (axs[1, 1], history[-1], plt.cm.Reds, "Final Distribution"),
    ]:
        _plot_density_heatmap(ax, points, cmap, title, x_range, y_range, "x", ylabel)

    plt.tight_layout()
    if save_path:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(save_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
        _LOGGER.info(f"Collocation evolution saved to {save_path}")
    plt.close(fig)

def save_training_plots(trainer, save_dir):  # pragma: no cover
    """Write every post-training figure into ``save_dir``.

    Each figure is attempted independently, so one failing plot never loses
    the others or crashes the run.
    """
    os.makedirs(save_dir, exist_ok=True)
    jobs = [
        ("final_training_history.png", plot_training_history, {}),
        ("final_solution_comparison.png", plot_solution_comparison, {"num_points": 100}),
        ("collocation_evolution.png", plot_collocation_evolution, {}),
    ]
    for filename, plot, kwargs in jobs:
        try:
            plot(trainer, save_path=os.path.join(save_dir, filename), **kwargs)
        except Exception as e:
            _LOGGER.warning(f"Could not write {filename}: {e}")

def __init__(
    self,
    domain: tuple[float, float],
    time_domain: tuple[float, float],
    n_x_cells: int = 16,
    n_t_cells: int = 8,
    policy_fraction: float = 0.5,
    temperature: float = 0.5,
    probe_cells: int = 32,
    probe_points: int = 8,
    probe_every: int = 1,

    device: torch.device | None = None,
):

    self.x_lo, self.x_hi = float(domain[0]), float(domain[1])
    self.t_lo, self.t_hi = float(time_domain[0]), float(time_domain[1])
    self.n_x_cells = n_x_cells
    self.n_t_cells = n_t_cells
    self.n_cells = n_x_cells * n_t_cells
    self.policy_fraction = policy_fraction
    self.temperature = temperature

    self.probe_points = probe_points

probe(pde, model, progress)

Probe random cells, push rewards to the agent, and return the state.

probe_points random points in each of min(probe_cells, n_cells) distinct cells are scored by |residual|. The state is [log10 mean, log10 max, log10 std, progress] over all probed values (the mean is the mean of the cell means); each cell's reward is its mean divided by that overall mean. Each transition is stored with next_state = state, which gamma = 0 ignores.

Source code in pinnrl/rl/bandit_sampler.py 
def probe(self, pde, model: torch.nn.Module, progress: float) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Probe random cells, push rewards to the agent, and return the state.

    ``probe_points`` random points in each of ``min(probe_cells, n_cells)``
    distinct cells are scored by ``|residual|``. The state is
    ``[log10 mean, log10 max, log10 std, progress]`` over all probed
    values (the mean is the mean of the cell means); each cell's reward
    is its mean divided by that overall mean. Each transition is stored
    with ``next_state = state``, which ``gamma = 0`` ignores.
    """
    cells = torch.randperm(self.n_cells, device=self.device)[: self.probe_cells]
    x, t = self._points_in_cells(cells.repeat_interleave(self.probe_points))
    residual = pde.compute_residual(model, x.requires_grad_(True), t.requires_grad_(True))
    res_abs = residual.detach().abs().reshape(len(cells), self.probe_points)

    cell_means = res_abs.mean(dim=1)
    overall = cell_means.mean().clamp_min(1e-12)
    state = torch.tensor(
        [
            torch.log10(overall).item(),
            torch.log10(res_abs.max().clamp_min(1e-12)).item(),
            torch.log10(res_abs.std().clamp_min(1e-12)).item(),
            float(progress),
        ],
        device=self.device,
    )
    for cell, reward in zip(cells.tolist(), (cell_means / overall).tolist(), strict=False):
        self.agent.update(state, cell, reward, state, False)
    return state

The Q-network is evaluated in eval mode (dropout off), so the same state always gives the same distribution.

Source code in pinnrl/rl/bandit_sampler.py 
def distribution(self, state: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """ε-mixture of ``softmax(Q / temperature)`` and the uniform distribution.

    The Q-network is evaluated in eval mode (dropout off), so the same
    state always gives the same distribution.
    """
    net = self.agent.policy_net
    was_training = net.training
    net.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        q = net(state.unsqueeze(0)).squeeze(0)
    net.train(was_training)
    eps = float(self.agent.epsilon)
    return (1.0 - eps) * torch.softmax(q / self.temperature, dim=0) + eps / self.n_cells

Return num_points collocation points, as (x, t) columns.

Source code in pinnrl/rl/bandit_sampler.py 
def sample(
    self, pde, model: torch.nn.Module, num_points: int, progress: float = 0.0
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Return ``num_points`` collocation points, as ``(x, t)`` columns.

    Probes and updates the agent first on every ``probe_every``-th call
    (and on the first); other calls reuse the last state. ``progress`` in
    [0, 1] is the training-progress entry of the state.
    """
    if self._state is None or self._calls % self.probe_every == 0:
        self._state = self.probe(pde, model, progress)
    self._calls += 1
    state = self._state
    n_policy = int(round(num_points * self.policy_fraction))
    if n_policy > 0:
        cells = torch.multinomial(self.distribution(state), n_policy, replacement=True)
    else:
        cells = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
    x_p, t_p = self._points_in_cells(cells)
    x_u, t_u = self._uniform(num_points - n_policy)
    return torch.cat([x_p, x_u]).detach(), torch.cat([t_p, t_u]).detach()

def __init__(
    self,
    state_dim: int,
    action_dim: int,
    hidden_dim: int,
    learning_rate: float = 0.0001,
    gamma: float = 0.99,
    epsilon_start: float = 1.0,
    epsilon_end: float = 0.01,
    epsilon_decay: float = 0.995,
    memory_size: int = 10000,
    batch_size: int = 64,
    target_update: int = 100,
    device: torch.device | None = None,
):
    """Initialize RL agent.

    Args:
        state_dim: State dimension.
        action_dim: Number of discrete actions.
        hidden_dim: Hidden layer dimension.
        learning_rate: Learning rate.
        gamma: Discount factor (``0`` turns the DQN into a contextual bandit).
        epsilon_start: Initial exploration rate.
        epsilon_end: Final exploration rate.
        epsilon_decay: Multiplicative ε decay applied on every :meth:`update`.
        memory_size: Size of replay buffer.
        batch_size: Batch size for training.
        target_update: Updates between target-network syncs.
        device: Device to place the networks on.
    """
    self.device = device or torch.device("cpu")
    self.state_dim = state_dim
    self.action_dim = action_dim
    self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
    self.learning_rate = learning_rate
    self.gamma = gamma
    self.epsilon = epsilon_start
    self.epsilon_end = epsilon_end
    self.epsilon_decay = epsilon_decay
    self.batch_size = batch_size
    self.target_update = target_update

    self.policy_net = DQNNetwork(state_dim, action_dim, hidden_dim).to(self.device)
    self.target_net = DQNNetwork(state_dim, action_dim, hidden_dim).to(self.device)
    self.target_net.load_state_dict(self.policy_net.state_dict())
    self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.policy_net.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
    self.memory = ReplayBuffer(memory_size)
    self.steps = 0

def update(
    self,
    state: torch.Tensor,
    action: int,
    reward: float,
    next_state: torch.Tensor,
    done: bool,
):
    """Store a transition, train on a replayed batch, and decay ε.

    Training starts once the buffer holds ``batch_size`` transitions; the
    target network is synced every ``target_update`` calls.

    Args:
        state: Current state.
        action: Action taken.
        reward: Reward received.
        next_state: Next state.
        done: Whether the episode ended.
    """
    self.memory.push(state, action, reward, next_state, done)
    self.steps += 1
    if self.steps % self.target_update == 0:
        self.target_net.load_state_dict(self.policy_net.state_dict())
    if len(self.memory) >= self.batch_size:
        self._train()
    self.epsilon = max(self.epsilon_end, self.epsilon * self.epsilon_decay)

def __init__(
    self,
    state_dim: int,
    action_dim: int,
    hidden_dim: int,
    num_layers: int = 3,
    dropout: float = 0.1,
):
    """Initialize DQN network.

    Args:
        state_dim: State dimension.
        action_dim: Action dimension.
        hidden_dim: Hidden layer dimension.
        num_layers: Number of linear layers, input and output included.
        dropout: Dropout rate after each hidden block.
    """
    super().__init__()

    # Build network
    layers = []

    # Input layer
    layers.append(
        nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(state_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )
    )

    # Hidden layers
    for _ in range(num_layers - 2):
        layers.append(
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(dropout),
            )
        )

    # Output layer
    layers.append(nn.Linear(hidden_dim, action_dim))

    self.layers = nn.Sequential(*layers)

    # Initialize weights
    self._init_weights()

def sample(self, batch_size: int) -> list[tuple]:
    """Sample a batch of experiences without replacement.

    Indices come from torch's generator, so ``torch.manual_seed`` makes
    the draw (and a bandit run) reproducible.

    Args:
        batch_size: Size of batch to sample.

    Returns:
        List of experiences.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``batch_size`` exceeds the stored experiences.
    """
    if batch_size > len(self.buffer):
        raise ValueError(
            f"batch_size {batch_size} exceeds the {len(self.buffer)} stored experiences"
        )
    return [self.buffer[i] for i in torch.randperm(len(self.buffer))[:batch_size].tolist()]

def __init__(
    self,
    model: nn.Module,
    pde: "PDEBase",
    config: "Config",
    device: torch.device | None = None,
    bandit_sampler=None,
):
    """Initialize trainer.

    Args:
        model: PINN model.
        pde: PDE instance.
        config: Full configuration object. Optimizer, scheduler, early
            stopping and loss settings all come from ``config.training``.
        device: Device to train on.
        bandit_sampler: Optional ``ResidualBanditSampler``. When given (or when
            ``collocation_distribution`` is ``"adaptive"``) collocation points
            come from the experimental RL bandit sampler.
    """
    # An explicit device wins, then config.device, then MPS if available, else CPU
    self.device = device or (
        config.device
        if hasattr(config, "device")
        else torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")
    )

    self.model = model.to(self.device)
    self.pde = pde
    self.config = config
    self.validation_frequency = config.training.validation_frequency

    # Setup logging up-front so optimizer init can warn through self.logger.
    self._setup_logging()

    # Setup optimizer
    self._num_epochs = config.training.num_epochs
    self._initialize_optimizer_and_scheduler()

    # Training history
    self.history = {
        "train_loss": [],
        "val_loss": [],
        "residual_loss": [],
        "boundary_loss": [],
        "initial_loss": [],
        "learning_rate": [],
        "loss_weights": [],  # adaptive weights at the end of each epoch that updated them
    }
    self._latest_loss_weights = None  # set by every adaptive step, recorded per epoch

    es_cfg = config.training.early_stopping
    self.early_stopping_enabled = es_cfg.enabled
    self.patience = es_cfg.patience
    self.min_delta = float(es_cfg.min_delta)
    self.best_val_loss = float("inf")
    self.patience_counter = 0

    self.use_rl = (
        bandit_sampler is not None
        or getattr(config.training, "collocation_distribution", None) == "adaptive"
    )
    if bandit_sampler is not None:
        pde.bandit_sampler = bandit_sampler

    # Initialize adaptive weights handler if enabled
    self.use_adaptive_weights = config.training.adaptive_weights.enabled
    if self.use_adaptive_weights:
        self.adaptive_weights = AdaptiveLossWeights(
            strategy=config.training.adaptive_weights.strategy,
            alpha=config.training.adaptive_weights.alpha,
            eps=config.training.adaptive_weights.eps,
            initial_weights=config.training.adaptive_weights.initial_weights,
        )
    else:
        self.logger.info("Adaptive weights are disabled")
        self.adaptive_weights = None

def setup_experiment_logging(self, experiment_dir=None):
    """Log to ``<experiment_dir>/experiment.log``, replacing earlier file handlers.

    Args:
        experiment_dir: Directory for the experiment; ``None`` is a no-op.
    """
    if experiment_dir:
        # Remove all FileHandlers from the logger
        for handler in self.logger.handlers[:]:
            if isinstance(handler, logging.FileHandler):
                self.logger.removeHandler(handler)

        # Add experiment-specific log file handler
        log_file = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "experiment.log")
        file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file)
        file_handler.setFormatter(
            logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s")
        )
        file_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)
        self.logger.addHandler(file_handler)
        # The run log records INFO even when the application logs at WARNING.
        if self.logger.getEffectiveLevel() > logging.INFO:
            self.logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
        self.logger.info(f"Experiment logs will be saved to {log_file}")

def train_steps(
    self,
    num_steps: int | None = None,
    time_budget_s: float | None = None,
    sample_fn: Callable | None = None,
    resample_every: int = 1,
    checkpoints: Sequence[float] = (),
    on_checkpoint: Callable | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Step-based training loop for benchmarks and studies.

    Runs :meth:`_step` (the same update as :meth:`train`) until
    ``num_steps`` steps or until training time reaches ``time_budget_s``.
    Training time is the summed wall-clock of sampling plus optimizer steps;
    checkpoint callbacks are excluded. There is no validation, early
    stopping, LR warm-up or scheduling, progress bar or disk I/O.

    Args:
        num_steps: Stop after this many steps.
        time_budget_s: Stop once training time reaches this many seconds.
        sample_fn: ``sample_fn(model, progress) -> (x, t)``, where ``progress``
            in [0, 1) is the elapsed fraction of the time budget (or of
            ``num_steps`` without one); defaults to the configured
            collocation strategy with ``config.training.batch_size``.
        resample_every: Draw new points every N steps and reuse them between.
        checkpoints: Increasing training-time marks (seconds).
        on_checkpoint: Called as ``on_checkpoint(step, train_time_s, model)``
            when training time first passes each mark.

    Returns:
        ``{"steps", "train_time_s", "loss"}`` with the per-step total loss.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither ``num_steps`` nor ``time_budget_s`` is given.
    """
    if num_steps is None and time_budget_s is None:
        raise ValueError("Pass num_steps, time_budget_s, or both.")
    if sample_fn is None:
        batch_size = self.config.training.batch_size

        def sample_fn(_model, progress):
            return self._sample_batch(batch_size, progress)

    pending = list(checkpoints)
    loss_curve = []
    clock = 0.0
    step = 0
    x_batch = t_batch = None
    self.model.train()
    while (num_steps is None or step < num_steps) and (
        time_budget_s is None or clock < time_budget_s
    ):
        if time_budget_s is not None:
            progress = clock / time_budget_s
        else:
            progress = step / num_steps
        start = time.perf_counter()
        if step % resample_every == 0:
            x_batch, t_batch = sample_fn(self.model, progress)
        losses = self._step(x_batch, t_batch)
        loss_value = float(losses["total"].item())  # syncs MPS/CUDA before the clock stops
        clock += time.perf_counter() - start
        step += 1
        loss_curve.append(loss_value)
        while pending and clock >= pending[0]:
            pending.pop(0)
            if on_checkpoint is not None:
                on_checkpoint(step, clock, self.model)
                self.model.train()
    return {"steps": step, "train_time_s": clock, "loss": loss_curve}

Train the model.

Each epoch takes max(1, num_points // batch_size) optimizer steps on freshly sampled batches (one full batch when optimizer is lbfgs). Every validation_frequency epochs (starting at epoch 0) it validates, logs, checks early stopping (patience counted in epochs) and, with experiment_dir, saves history, metadata and the live snapshot.

Each call is planned as its own run: the learning rate restarts at training.learning_rate and the schedule and the Adam -> L-BFGS switch are sized to num_epochs. Weights, optimizer moments and history carry over from earlier calls.

def train(
    self,
    num_epochs: int | None = None,
    batch_size: int | None = None,
    num_points: int | None = None,
    experiment_dir: str | None = None,
    progress: bool = True,
):
    """Train the model.

    Each epoch takes ``max(1, num_points // batch_size)`` optimizer steps on
    freshly sampled batches (one full batch when ``optimizer`` is ``lbfgs``). Every
    ``validation_frequency`` epochs (starting at epoch 0) it validates,
    logs, checks early stopping (patience counted in epochs) and, with
    ``experiment_dir``, saves history, metadata and the live snapshot.

    Each call is planned as its own run: the learning rate restarts at
    ``training.learning_rate`` and the schedule and the Adam -> L-BFGS
    switch are sized to ``num_epochs``. Weights, optimizer moments and
    history carry over from earlier calls.

    Args:
        num_epochs: Defaults to ``config.training.num_epochs``.
        batch_size: Defaults to ``config.training.batch_size``; capped at
            ``num_points``.
        num_points: Collocation points per epoch; defaults to
            ``config.training.num_collocation_points``.
        experiment_dir: Run folder for ``experiment.log``, ``metadata.json``,
            ``metrics.json``/``history.json``, ``live_snapshot.npz``,
            ``final_model.pt`` and ``visualizations/``; ``None`` writes nothing.
        progress: Show one tqdm progress bar over epochs.

    Returns:
        The training history dict (``self.history``).
    """
    training_cfg = self.config.training
    num_epochs = training_cfg.num_epochs if num_epochs is None else num_epochs
    batch_size = training_cfg.batch_size if batch_size is None else batch_size
    num_points = training_cfg.num_collocation_points if num_points is None else num_points
    if num_points < batch_size:
        batch_size = num_points
    # Each call is its own run: the LR restarts and cosine T_max and the
    # L-BFGS switch follow num_epochs. Weights and optimizer moments carry over.
    self._plan_epochs(num_epochs)
    self.model.train()
    if hasattr(self.model, "architecture_name"):
        architecture_name = self.model.architecture_name
    else:
        architecture_name = self.model.__class__.__name__

    # Log PDE and architecture information
    self.logger.info("=" * 50)
    self.logger.info(f"STARTING TRAINING FOR PDE: {self.pde.__class__.__name__}")
    self.logger.info(f"NEURAL NETWORK ARCHITECTURE: {architecture_name}")
    if hasattr(self.model, "model"):
        self.logger.info(f"MODEL STRUCTURE: {self.model.model}")
    self.logger.info(f"DEVICE: {self.device}")

    # Log adaptive weights configuration if enabled
    if self.use_adaptive_weights:
        self.logger.info("ADAPTIVE WEIGHTS ENABLED")
        self.logger.info(f"  Strategy: {self.config.training.adaptive_weights.strategy}")
        self.logger.info(f"  Alpha: {self.config.training.adaptive_weights.alpha}")
        self.logger.info(f"  Epsilon: {self.config.training.adaptive_weights.eps}")
    else:
        self.logger.info("ADAPTIVE WEIGHTS DISABLED")
        # Convert loss_weights to something printable
        weights_dict = {
            k: float(v) if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor) else v
            for k, v in self.config.training.loss_weights.items()
        }
        self.logger.info(f"  Fixed weights: {weights_dict}")
    self.logger.info("=" * 50)

    # Inverse-problem warm-up: announce trainable parameters and seed history
    # buckets so the dashboard can render trajectories from epoch 0.
    trainable_pde_params = {}
    if hasattr(self.pde, "_trainable_params"):
        trainable_pde_params = dict(self.pde._trainable_params)
    if trainable_pde_params:
        self.logger.info(
            "INVERSE MODE — identifying %d PDE parameter(s): %s",
            len(trainable_pde_params),
            list(trainable_pde_params.keys()),
        )
        for name in trainable_pde_params:
            self.history.setdefault(f"param_{name}", [])

    # L-BFGS requires deterministic full-batch loss; override batch_size
    # (the L-BFGS phase of adam_lbfgs does the same when it starts).
    if getattr(self, "_is_lbfgs", False) and batch_size != num_points:
        self.logger.warning(
            "L-BFGS optimizer requires full-batch updates; "
            f"overriding batch_size {batch_size} -> {num_points}."
        )
        batch_size = num_points

    # Adaptive weights are incompatible with the L-BFGS closure (per-component
    # gradient passes are too expensive); _step skips them during L-BFGS.
    if getattr(self, "_is_lbfgs", False) and self.use_adaptive_weights:
        self.logger.warning("Adaptive loss weighting is disabled while running L-BFGS.")

    # Record start time
    start_time = datetime.now()

    # Fields shared by the initial and the final metadata.json.
    run_info = {
        "pde_type": getattr(self.pde, "pde_type", type(self.pde).__name__),
        "pde_name": getattr(self.pde.config, "name", ""),
        "architecture": getattr(self.model, "architecture_name", type(self.model).__name__),
        "training_params": {
            "num_epochs": num_epochs,
            "batch_size": batch_size,
            "num_points": num_points,
            "validation_frequency": self.validation_frequency,
        },
        "collocation_distribution": (
            "adaptive" if self.use_rl else self.config.training.collocation_distribution
        ),
        "rl_enabled": self.use_rl,
        "optimizer": self._optimizer_type,
        "mode": self.config.training.mode,
        "trainable_parameters": list(trainable_pde_params.keys()),
        "true_parameters": dict(getattr(self.pde, "_true_parameters", {})),
    }

    # Create directories for visualizations and experiment data
    if experiment_dir:
        os.makedirs(experiment_dir, exist_ok=True)

        # Setup experiment-specific logging
        self.setup_experiment_logging(experiment_dir)

        # Create visualization directory
        viz_dir = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "visualizations")
        os.makedirs(viz_dir, exist_ok=True)

        # Create .running marker file
        running_file = os.path.join(experiment_dir, ".running")
        open(running_file, "w").close()

        initial_metadata = {
            "status": "running",
            "start_time": start_time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
            "total_epochs": num_epochs,
            "current_epoch": 0,
            **run_info,
        }
        metadata_path = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "metadata.json")
        with open(metadata_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(initial_metadata, f, indent=2)

    self.logger.info("Starting training...")

    # Initialize points history
    self.points_history = []

    # Emit an initial live snapshot so the Monitor tab has something to show
    # before the first epoch finishes.
    if experiment_dir:
        self._save_live_snapshot(experiment_dir, epoch=0)

    # tqdm.auto renders a widget in notebooks; refresh at most twice a second.
    pbar = tqdm(total=num_epochs, desc="Training", mininterval=0.5) if progress else None
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        self.model.train()
        self._apply_warmup(epoch)
        epoch_losses = []
        epoch_points = []  # Store all points for this epoch
        self._latest_loss_weights = None

        for _ in range(max(1, num_points // batch_size)):
            x_batch, t_batch = self._sample_batch(batch_size, epoch / max(1, num_epochs))
            epoch_points.append(torch.cat([x_batch, t_batch], dim=1).detach().cpu().numpy())
            losses = self._step(x_batch, t_batch)
            epoch_losses.append(float(losses["total"].item()))
        # L-BFGS epochs do not weight adaptively and record nothing; they
        # come after the Adam epochs, so the recorded epochs stay a prefix.
        if self._latest_loss_weights is not None:
            self.history["loss_weights"].append(self._latest_loss_weights)
        if pbar is not None:
            pbar.set_postfix(
                loss=f"{epoch_losses[-1]:.3e}",
                res=f"{losses['residual'].item():.3e}",
                refresh=False,
            )
            pbar.update()

        # End of epoch
        avg_epoch_loss = sum(epoch_losses) / len(epoch_losses)
        points_array = np.concatenate(epoch_points, axis=0)
        self.points_history.append(points_array)

        # Update learning rate (the scheduler takes over after warm-up)
        if epoch >= self._warmup_epochs():
            self._update_scheduler(avg_epoch_loss)

        # Log metrics
        current_lr = self.optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"]

        epoch_data = {
            "epoch": epoch,
            "train_loss": avg_epoch_loss,
            "residual_loss": _as_float(losses["residual"]),
            "boundary_loss": _as_float(losses["boundary"]),
            "initial_loss": _as_float(losses["initial"]),
            "learning_rate": current_lr,
        }
        if "data" in losses:
            epoch_data["data_loss"] = _as_float(losses["data"])
            self.history.setdefault("data_loss", [])

        # Capture each trainable PDE parameter's current value so the
        # dashboard can plot its trajectory in real time.
        if trainable_pde_params:
            for name, p in trainable_pde_params.items():
                epoch_data[f"param_{name}"] = float(p.detach().cpu().item())

        # Add weights info if using adaptive weights
        if self.use_adaptive_weights and len(self.history["loss_weights"]) > 0:
            current_weights = self.history["loss_weights"][-1]
            weights_str = ""
            component_names = ["residual", "boundary", "initial"]
            for i, name in enumerate(component_names):
                if i < len(current_weights):
                    weights_str += f", {name}_weight={float(current_weights[i]):.4f}"

        else:
            weights_str = ""

        # Update history
        for key, value in epoch_data.items():
            if key in self.history:
                self.history[key].append(value)

        # Validation (if applicable)
        if epoch % self.validation_frequency == 0:
            val_losses = self._compute_validation_loss()
            self.history["val_loss"].append(val_losses["total_loss"])
            self.logger.info(
                f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{num_epochs}, "
                f"Train Loss: {avg_epoch_loss:.6f}, "
                f"Val Loss: {val_losses['total_loss']:.6f}, "
                f"LR: {current_lr:.6f}{weights_str}"
            )

            # Early stopping check
            if self.early_stopping_enabled:
                val_loss = val_losses["total_loss"]
                if val_loss < self.best_val_loss - self.min_delta:
                    self.best_val_loss = val_loss
                    self.patience_counter = 0
                else:
                    # Patience is in epochs; validation runs every validation_frequency.
                    self.patience_counter += self.validation_frequency

                if self.patience_counter >= self.patience:
                    self.logger.info(
                        f"Early stopping triggered at epoch {epoch + 1}, "
                        f"best val loss: {self.best_val_loss:.6f}"
                    )
                    break

        # Periodic save of history and metadata
        if experiment_dir and epoch % self.validation_frequency == 0:
            save_training_metrics(self.history, experiment_dir)
            metadata_path = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "metadata.json")
            try:
                with open(metadata_path) as f:
                    partial_metadata = json.load(f)
            except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
                partial_metadata = {}
            partial_metadata.update(
                {
                    "current_epoch": epoch + 1,
                    "status": "running",
                    "final_loss": float(avg_epoch_loss),
                    "best_val_loss": (
                        float(self.best_val_loss)
                        if self.best_val_loss != float("inf")
                        else None
                    ),
                    "last_updated": datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                }
            )
            if trainable_pde_params:
                partial_metadata["current_parameters"] = {
                    name: float(p.detach().cpu().item())
                    for name, p in trainable_pde_params.items()
                }
            with open(metadata_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(partial_metadata, f, indent=2)
            # Refresh the live 3D snapshot for the dashboard.
            self._save_live_snapshot(experiment_dir, epoch=epoch + 1)

        # adam_lbfgs: hot-swap the optimizer once we cross the switch boundary.
        if (
            getattr(self, "_optimizer_type", "adam") == "adam_lbfgs"
            and not self._is_lbfgs
            and self._switch_epoch is not None
            and (epoch + 1) >= self._switch_epoch
        ):
            self.logger.info(f"Switching optimizer to L-BFGS at epoch {epoch + 1}")
            self._switch_to_lbfgs()
            batch_size = num_points  # L-BFGS needs the full batch
            if self.use_adaptive_weights:
                self.logger.warning("Adaptive loss weighting is disabled while running L-BFGS.")

    if pbar is not None:
        pbar.close()

    # End of training
    train_time = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds() / 60.0
    self.logger.info(f"Training completed in {train_time} minutes")

    # Save final visualizations and metrics
    if experiment_dir:
        # Create metadata with training information
        metadata = {
            **run_info,
            "status": "completed",
            "training_time_minutes": train_time,
            "total_epochs": num_epochs,
            "final_loss": (
                float(self.history["train_loss"][-1]) if self.history["train_loss"] else None
            ),
            "best_val_loss": (
                float(self.best_val_loss) if self.best_val_loss != float("inf") else None
            ),
            "early_stopping_triggered": (
                self.patience_counter >= self.patience if self.early_stopping_enabled else False
            ),
            "current_epoch": len(self.history["train_loss"]),
            "start_time": start_time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
            "end_time": datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
            "domain": self.pde.domain,
            "time_domain": self.pde.time_domain,
            "boundary_conditions": self.pde.config.boundary_conditions,
            "initial_condition": self.pde.config.initial_condition,
            "pde_parameters": self.pde.config.parameters,
            "identified_parameters": (
                self.pde.get_trainable_parameter_values() if trainable_pde_params else {}
            ),
        }

        # Save training history as metrics.json and history.json
        self.logger.info("Saving training metrics...")
        save_training_metrics(self.history, experiment_dir, metadata=metadata)

        # Final live snapshot reflects the trained model.
        self._save_live_snapshot(experiment_dir, epoch=len(self.history.get("train_loss", [])))

        # Remove .running marker
        running_file = os.path.join(experiment_dir, ".running")
        if os.path.exists(running_file):
            try:
                os.remove(running_file)
            except OSError:
                pass

        # Save the model directly in the experiment directory
        self.logger.info("Saving model...")
        model_path = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "final_model.pt")
        torch.save(self.model.state_dict(), model_path)

        # Save all plots using the save_plots method
        self.logger.info("Generating and saving all plots...")
        self.save_plots(viz_dir)

    return self.history

def save_training_metrics(
    history: dict[str, Any],
    experiment_dir: str,
    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
):
    """Save training metrics to JSON files.

    Writes the same history to ``metrics.json`` and ``history.json``. When
    ``metadata`` is given it is merged into an existing ``metadata.json`` and
    stamped with ``last_updated``.

    Args:
        history: Dictionary containing training metrics
        experiment_dir: Directory to save the metrics
        metadata: Optional metadata about the experiment

    Returns:
        Path of ``history.json``.
    """
    # Create experiment directory if it doesn't exist
    os.makedirs(experiment_dir, exist_ok=True)

    # Convert NumPy arrays to Python lists in history
    def convert_to_serializable(obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()
        elif isinstance(obj, dict):
            return {k: convert_to_serializable(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
        elif isinstance(obj, list):
            return [convert_to_serializable(item) for item in obj]
        return obj

    serializable_history = convert_to_serializable(history)

    # Save metrics.json directly in the experiment directory
    metrics_file = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "metrics.json")
    with open(metrics_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump(serializable_history, f, indent=2)

    # Save history.json directly in the experiment directory
    history_file = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "history.json")
    with open(history_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump(serializable_history, f, indent=2)

    # Save metadata if provided
    if metadata:
        metadata_file = os.path.join(experiment_dir, "metadata.json")

        # Update existing metadata if it exists
        if os.path.exists(metadata_file):
            try:
                with open(metadata_file) as f:
                    existing_metadata = json.load(f)
                # Update with new metadata
                existing_metadata.update(metadata)
                metadata = existing_metadata
            except Exception:
                pass

        # Add timestamp
        metadata["last_updated"] = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

        # Convert metadata to serializable format
        serializable_metadata = convert_to_serializable(metadata)

        with open(metadata_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump(serializable_metadata, f, indent=2)

    return history_file

def __init__(self, strategy="rbw", alpha=0.9, eps=1e-5, initial_weights=None):
    """Initialize adaptive loss weights handler.

    Args:
        strategy (str): Weight adaptation strategy ('lrw' or 'rbw').
        alpha (float): EMA retention factor: ``new = alpha * old + (1 - alpha) * current``.
        eps (float): Small constant for numerical stability.
        initial_weights (list | None): Weights for [residual, boundary, initial]
            returned by the first update; ``None`` means ones.
    """
    self.strategy = strategy.lower()
    self.alpha = alpha
    # Ensure eps is a float, not a string
    self.eps = float(eps) if isinstance(eps, (str, int)) else eps
    self.initial_weights = (
        torch.tensor(initial_weights) if initial_weights is not None else None
    )
    self.weights = None
    self.running_losses = None
    self.running_grads = None
    self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    self.logger.info(
        f"AdaptiveLossWeights initialized with strategy={strategy}, alpha={alpha}, eps={self.eps}, initial_weights={initial_weights}"
    )
    self.prev_weights = None

update_weights_lrw(gradients)

Update weights using Learning Rate based Weighting (LRW).

After the first call (which only seeds g_bar)::

g_bar_i = alpha * g_bar_i + (1 - alpha) * g_i
w_i = (1 / (g_bar_i + eps)) / sum_{j active} (1 / (g_bar_j + eps))

over the active components (g_bar_i > 0), so components with smaller gradient norms get larger weights. A component whose gradient norm is zero (a constant loss, e.g. a PDE with no boundary conditions) gets weight 0: it cannot be minimised, and 1 / eps would otherwise hand it almost all the weight and switch the other terms off. If no component is active the weights are uniform.

def update_weights_lrw(self, gradients):
    """Update weights using Learning Rate based Weighting (LRW).

    After the first call (which only seeds ``g_bar``)::

        g_bar_i = alpha * g_bar_i + (1 - alpha) * g_i
        w_i = (1 / (g_bar_i + eps)) / sum_{j active} (1 / (g_bar_j + eps))

    over the *active* components (``g_bar_i > 0``), so components with smaller
    gradient norms get larger weights. A component whose gradient norm is zero
    (a constant loss, e.g. a PDE with no boundary conditions) gets weight 0:
    it cannot be minimised, and ``1 / eps`` would otherwise hand it almost all
    the weight and switch the other terms off. If no component is active the
    weights are uniform.

    Args:
        gradients (torch.Tensor): Gradient norm of each loss component, shape ``(n,)``.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor: The weights, shape ``(n,)``.
    """
    if self.running_grads is None:
        self.running_grads = gradients
        self.weights = (
            self.initial_weights.to(gradients.device)
            if self.initial_weights is not None
            else torch.ones_like(gradients)
        )
        self.logger.debug(f"LRW - Initialized weights: {self.weights}")
        return self.weights

    # Update running average of gradients
    self.running_grads = self.alpha * self.running_grads + (1 - self.alpha) * gradients

    # Ensure eps is a tensor on the same device as the gradients
    eps_tensor = torch.tensor(self.eps, device=self.running_grads.device)

    # Inverse-gradient weights over the components that have a gradient at all.
    active = self.running_grads > 0
    if not torch.any(active):
        self.weights = torch.full_like(self.running_grads, 1.0 / len(self.running_grads))
    else:
        inv_grads = torch.where(
            active,
            1.0 / (self.running_grads + eps_tensor),
            torch.zeros_like(self.running_grads),
        )
        self.weights = inv_grads / torch.sum(inv_grads)

    self.logger.debug(
        f"LRW - Updated weights: gradients={gradients.detach().cpu().numpy()}, running_grads={self.running_grads.detach().cpu().numpy()}, weights={self.weights.detach().cpu().numpy()}"
    )

    return self.weights

def update_weights_rbw(self, losses):
    """Update weights using Relative Error based Weighting (RBW).

    Gives more weight to terms with bigger losses. After the first call
    (which only seeds ``L_bar``)::

        L_bar_i = alpha * L_bar_i + (1 - alpha) * L_i
        w_i = alpha * w_prev_i + (1 - alpha) * L_bar_i / (sum_j L_bar_j + eps)

    where ``w_prev`` is the previous RBW result; on the second call there is
    none yet and ``w_i`` is the normalised term alone.

    Args:
        losses (torch.Tensor): Detached value of each loss component, shape ``(n,)``.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor: The weights, shape ``(n,)``.
    """
    if self.running_losses is None:
        self.running_losses = losses
        self.weights = (
            self.initial_weights.to(losses.device)
            if self.initial_weights is not None
            else torch.ones_like(losses)
        )
        self.logger.info(f"RBW - Initialized weights: {self.weights}")
        return self.weights

    # Update running average of losses
    self.running_losses = self.alpha * self.running_losses + (1 - self.alpha) * losses

    # Ensure eps is a tensor on the same device as the losses
    eps_tensor = torch.tensor(self.eps, device=self.running_losses.device)

    # Normalize the running losses to get weights
    # Give more weight to higher losses to focus optimization on problematic terms
    normalized_losses = self.running_losses / (self.running_losses.sum() + eps_tensor)
    self.weights = normalized_losses  # Higher loss -> Higher weight

    # Update weights with exponential moving average
    if self.prev_weights is not None:
        self.weights = self.alpha * self.prev_weights + (1 - self.alpha) * self.weights

    self.prev_weights = self.weights.clone()

    self.logger.debug(
        f"RBW - Updated weights: losses={losses.detach().cpu().numpy()}, running_losses={self.running_losses.detach().cpu().numpy()}, weights={self.weights.detach().cpu().numpy()}"
    )

    return self.weights

def update(self, losses=None, gradients=None):
    """Update weights based on chosen strategy.

    Args:
        losses (torch.Tensor | None): Loss component values (required for ``rbw``).
        gradients (torch.Tensor | None): Gradient norm per component (required for ``lrw``).

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor: Updated loss weights.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the input the strategy needs is missing, or the strategy is unknown.
    """
    if self.strategy == "lrw" and gradients is not None:
        return self.update_weights_lrw(gradients)
    elif self.strategy == "rbw" and losses is not None:
        return self.update_weights_rbw(losses)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid combination of strategy ({self.strategy}) and inputs")

def build_model(config_dict, device):
    """Build the PINNModel described by a ``build_config_dict`` result.

    Returns:
        ``(model, config)`` with the model on ``device`` and the
        :class:`~pinnrl.config.Config` it was built from.
    """
    arch_type = config_dict["model"]["architecture"]
    config_obj = Config()
    config_obj.device = device
    config_obj.model = ModelConfig.from_architecture(
        arch_type,
        config_dict["architectures"].get(arch_type, {}),
        input_dim=config_dict["model"]["input_dim"],
        output_dim=config_dict["model"]["output_dim"],
    )
    config_obj.training = TrainingConfig.from_dict(config_dict["training"])
    return PINNModel(config=config_obj, device=device).to(device), config_obj

def load_run(run_dir, device=None):
    """Rebuild the PDE and trained model of a finished run.

    Reads the run's ``config.yaml`` snapshot and ``final_model.pt`` and goes
    through the same builders as :func:`run_training`, so the result matches
    what was trained. The PDE is the forward problem at the configured (true)
    parameters, so its exact solution is the reference even for inverse runs;
    observation data is not reloaded (a Well run's snapshot records the time
    window its observations covered).

    Args:
        run_dir: Run folder written by :func:`run_training`.
        device: Torch device; defaults to CPU.

    Returns:
        ``(pde, model, config_dict)`` with the model in eval mode.
    """
    device = device or torch.device("cpu")
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    with open(run_dir / "config.yaml") as f:
        config_dict = yaml.safe_load(f)
    pde_only = {
        **config_dict,
        "pde": {
            **config_dict["pde"],
            "observation_data": None,
            "trainable_parameters": [],
            "parameter_initial_guesses": {},
        },
    }
    pde_only["training"] = {**config_dict["training"], "mode": "forward"}
    pde = create_pde(pde_only, device)
    model, _ = build_model(config_dict, device)
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(run_dir / "final_model.pt", map_location=device))
    model.eval()
    return pde, model, config_dict

Gaussian posterior over parameters at the trained estimate.

The covariance is the inverse Fisher information of the surrogate's sensitivities at the observation points (pde.observation_data by default, or x, t). This is the Laplace approximation restricted to the parameters with the generalized Gauss–Newton curvature; it coincides with the Cramér–Rao bound at the estimate.

def laplace_posterior(
    pde: Any,
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    parameters: Sequence[str],
    sigma: float | torch.Tensor,
    x: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    t: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    **sensitivity_kwargs: Any,
) -> LaplacePosterior:
    """Gaussian posterior over ``parameters`` at the trained estimate.

    The covariance is the inverse Fisher information of the surrogate's
    sensitivities at the observation points (``pde.observation_data`` by
    default, or ``x, t``). This is the Laplace approximation restricted to the
    parameters with the generalized Gauss–Newton curvature; it coincides with
    the Cramér–Rao bound at the estimate.
    """
    if x is None:
        obs = pde.observation_data
        if obs is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "laplace_posterior needs observation points: pde.observation_data or x, t"
            )
        x, t = obs["x"], obs["t"]
    sens = surrogate_sensitivities(pde, model, parameters, x, t, **sensitivity_kwargs)
    summary = fisher_information(sens.jacobian, sigma, parameters)
    values = pde.get_trainable_parameter_values()
    mean = torch.tensor(
        [values.get(n, _scalar(pde.get_parameter(n))) for n in parameters], dtype=torch.float64
    )
    return LaplacePosterior(
        parameters=tuple(parameters),
        mean=mean,
        covariance=summary.covariance,
        std=summary.std,
        correlation=summary.correlation,
    )

def interval(self, level: float = 0.9) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Central interval per parameter, ``(2, p)``."""
    from pinnrl.uq.metrics import _normal_quantile

def sample(self, n: int, seed: int = 0) -> torch.Tensor:
    """``n`` draws, ``(n, p)``."""
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    L = torch.linalg.cholesky(self.covariance)
    z = torch.randn(n, self.mean.numel(), generator=gen, dtype=self.covariance.dtype)
    return self.mean.double() + z @ L.T

def likelihood_weights(
    n_data: int,
    sigma_data: float,
    n_residual: int,
    sigma_residual: float = 1.0,
    *,
    boundary: float = 10.0,
    initial: float = 10.0,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Loss weights that make the mean-squared loss a negative log-likelihood up to scale.

    The loss uses means, so a term with ``n`` points and noise ``sigma``
    contributes ``n / (2 sigma^2)`` times its mean square to ``-log L``. With
    the residual weight fixed at 1, the data weight is
    ``(n_data / sigma_data^2) / (n_residual / sigma_residual^2)``, where
    ``sigma_residual`` is the model-error scale admitted for the equation.
    """
    data = (n_data / sigma_data**2) / (n_residual / sigma_residual**2)
    return {"residual": 1.0, "boundary": boundary, "initial": initial, "data": float(data)}

def sample_equivalence_region(
    misfit: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray],
    bounds: Sequence[tuple[float, float]],
    tolerance: float | None = None,
    *,
    sigma: float | None = None,
    level: float = 0.9,
    n_particles: int = 40,
    n_iterations: int = 100,
    seed: int = 0,
    exploration: float = 0.9,
    stop_on_collapse: float = 0.02,
) -> SwarmSample:
    """Sample ``{theta : misfit(theta) <= tolerance}`` with a cloud particle swarm.

    Args:
        misfit: Vectorized misfit, ``(n, p) -> (n,)``. For Gaussian noise use
            the sum of squared residuals over ``sigma^2`` and a tolerance of
            about ``N (1 + epsilon)``; see :func:`misfit_tolerance`.
        bounds: ``(low, high)`` per parameter: the prior range, which the
            swarm explores and particles are reflected into.
        tolerance: Accept positions with misfit at or below it. When ``None``,
            the likelihood-ratio region is used instead: positions within
            ``sigma^2 chi2_p(level)`` of the best misfit found, which for
            Gaussian noise is the asymptotic ``level`` confidence region and
            is directly comparable with the Fisher ellipse at that level.
        sigma: Noise standard deviation, needed when ``tolerance`` is ``None``
            and the misfit is a plain sum of squares (use ``1`` if the misfit
            is already divided by ``sigma^2``).
        level: Confidence level of the likelihood-ratio region.
        n_particles: Swarm size.
        n_iterations: Iterations; every evaluation is a candidate sample.
        seed: Seed of the initial positions and of the per-particle parameters.
        exploration: Fraction of the way to the second-order stability border
            at which each particle's acceleration is drawn (close to 1 is the
            exploratory setting the papers recommend).
        stop_on_collapse: Stop when the dispersion falls below this fraction
            of its initial value.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    lo = np.asarray([b[0] for b in bounds], dtype=float)
    hi = np.asarray([b[1] for b in bounds], dtype=float)
    p = lo.size
    x = lo + (hi - lo) * rng.random((n_particles, p))
    v = np.zeros_like(x)
    # Cloud parameters: inertia in [0.5, 0.95], total acceleration a fraction of
    # the way to the variance-stability border, time step in [0.8, 1.2].
    omega = rng.uniform(0.5, 0.95, n_particles)
    phi_max = 12 * (1 - omega**2) / (7 - 5 * omega)
    phi = exploration * phi_max * rng.uniform(0.8, 1.0, n_particles)
    dt = rng.uniform(0.8, 1.2, n_particles)

    f = np.asarray(misfit(x), dtype=float)
    local_best, local_f = x.copy(), f.copy()
    g_idx = int(np.argmin(f))
    global_best, global_f = x[g_idx].copy(), float(f[g_idx])
    positions, misfits = [x.copy()], [f.copy()]
    centre = np.median(x, axis=0)
    d0 = float(np.median(np.linalg.norm(x - centre, axis=1))) or 1.0
    dispersion = [1.0]
    for _ in range(1, n_iterations):
        r1, r2 = rng.random((n_particles, p)), rng.random((n_particles, p))
        a_g = phi[:, None] * r1  # each particle's accelerations sum to phi on average
        a_l = phi[:, None] * r2
        # Generalized PSO with time step dt: damping (1 - omega) dt, stiffness phi dt^2.
        v = (1 - (1 - omega[:, None]) * dt[:, None]) * v + dt[:, None] * (
            a_g * (global_best - x) + a_l * (local_best - x)
        )
        x = x + dt[:, None] * v
        # Reflect into the bounds.
        below, above = x < lo, x > hi
        x = np.where(below, 2 * lo - x, x)
        x = np.where(above, 2 * hi - x, x)
        x = np.clip(x, lo, hi)
        v = np.where(below | above, -v, v)
        f = np.asarray(misfit(x), dtype=float)
        improved = f < local_f
        local_best[improved], local_f[improved] = x[improved], f[improved]
        i = int(np.argmin(local_f))
        if local_f[i] < global_f:
            global_best, global_f = local_best[i].copy(), float(local_f[i])
        positions.append(x.copy())
        misfits.append(f.copy())
        centre = np.median(x, axis=0)
        dispersion.append(float(np.median(np.linalg.norm(x - centre, axis=1))) / d0)
        if dispersion[-1] < stop_on_collapse:
            break
    P = np.concatenate(positions)
    M = np.concatenate(misfits)
    if tolerance is None:
        if sigma is None:
            raise ValueError("give a tolerance, or sigma for the likelihood-ratio region")
        tolerance = global_f + sigma**2 * chi2_quantile(p, level)
    return SwarmSample(
        positions=P,
        misfits=M,
        accepted=M <= tolerance,
        best=global_best,
        best_misfit=global_f,
        dispersion=np.asarray(dispersion),
        tolerance=tolerance,
    )

def misfit_tolerance(n_observations: int, sigma: float, epsilon: float = 0.1) -> float:
    """Tolerance on the squared misfit ``sum (y - u)^2`` for Gaussian noise.

    The expected squared misfit of the true parameters is ``N sigma^2``; the

For the classical PSO with uniformly distributed accelerations the mean trajectory is stable for |omega| < 1 and 0 < phi < 2 (omega + 1), and the variance for phi < 12 (1 - omega^2) / (7 - 5 omega) (Poli, 2009; García-Gonzalo & Fernández-Martínez, 2014, for general distributions). phi is the mean total acceleration (a_g + a_l) / 2.

def second_order_stable(omega: float, phi: float) -> bool:
    """Whether a PSO parameter pair is inside the second-order (variance) stability region.

    For the classical PSO with uniformly distributed accelerations the mean
    trajectory is stable for ``|omega| < 1`` and ``0 < phi < 2 (omega + 1)``, and
    the variance for ``phi < 12 (1 - omega^2) / (7 - 5 omega)`` (Poli, 2009;
    García-Gonzalo & Fernández-Martínez, 2014, for general distributions).
    ``phi`` is the mean total acceleration ``(a_g + a_l) / 2``.
    """
    return abs(omega) < 1 and 0 < phi < 12 * (1 - omega**2) / (7 - 5 * omega)

def ensemble_summary(estimates: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> EnsembleSummary:
    """Summarize the estimates of an ensemble of independently trained members."""
    e = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(estimates, dtype=float))
    med = np.median(e, axis=0)
    scale = float(np.mean(np.abs(med))) or 1.0
    return EnsembleSummary(
        estimates=e,
        mean=e.mean(axis=0),
        std=e.std(axis=0, ddof=1) if e.shape[0] > 1 else np.zeros(e.shape[1]),
        dispersion=float(np.median(np.linalg.norm(e - med, axis=1))) / scale,
    )

Continuous ranked probability score of a Gaussian forecast (Gneiting & Raftery, 2007).

CRPS = sigma [ z (2 Phi(z) - 1) + 2 phi(z) - 1/sqrt(pi) ] with z = (y - mu) / sigma. Lower is better; it rewards both calibration and sharpness.

Source code in pinnrl/uq/metrics.py 
def crps_gaussian(mean: float, std: float, truth: float) -> float:
    """Continuous ranked probability score of a Gaussian forecast (Gneiting & Raftery, 2007).

    ``CRPS = sigma [ z (2 Phi(z) - 1) + 2 phi(z) - 1/sqrt(pi) ]`` with ``z = (y - mu) / sigma``.
    Lower is better; it rewards both calibration and sharpness.
    """
    if std <= 0:
        return abs(truth - mean)
    z = (truth - mean) / std
    phi = math.exp(-0.5 * z * z) / math.sqrt(2 * math.pi)
    Phi = 0.5 * (1 + math.erf(z / math.sqrt(2)))
    return std * (z * (2 * Phi - 1) + 2 * phi - 1 / math.sqrt(math.pi))

docs.title: crps_samples
docs.text:
crps_samples(samples, truth)

CRPS of an empirical forecast: E|X - y| - E|X - X'| / 2.

Source code in pinnrl/uq/metrics.py 
def crps_samples(samples: Sequence[float], truth: float) -> float:
    """CRPS of an empirical forecast: ``E|X - y| - E|X - X'| / 2``."""
    s = np.asarray(samples, dtype=float)
    term1 = float(np.mean(np.abs(s - truth)))
    term2 = float(np.mean(np.abs(s[:, None] - s[None, :])))
    return term1 - 0.5 * term2

docs.title: Theory
docs.text:
The point of pinnrl is to estimate unknown physics from measurements and to say how far the estimate can be trusted. That claim rests on conditions, and the pages here state them. Each module of the inverse-modelling core cites the condition it relies on, so that a number the package reports comes with the assumption that makes it meaningful.

Page Question it answers Used by Well-posedness and stability When does a small change in the data give a small change in the estimate, and what does the physics do to an ill-posed problem? the disturbance suite, the stability constants Identifiability and conditioning Can the sensors determine the parameters at all, and which combinations do they determine badly? pinnrl.analysis, experiments F01–F05 and K01 The Bayesian view and uncertainty Why is the PINN loss a negative log-posterior, what does that make the loss weights, and what counts as a calibrated error bar? pinnrl.uq, K39, F06, K10 The numerical-analysis bridge What do consistency, stability and convergence mean for a PINN, and how does its error relate to the training residual? the error estimates, K06–K08 Equivalence regions and swarm sampling Why report the set of parameters that fit the data rather than one estimate, and how to sample it when the problem is nonlinear? pinnrl.uq, K10, K45–K48

The pages are short on purpose. They give the statement, the condition, the consequence for a PINN, and the reference where the proof lives. The notation is shared: \(u\) is the state, \(\theta\) the parameters to identify, \(\mathcal{N}_\theta[u] = 0\) the governing equation, \(y = \mathcal{H}u + \varepsilon\) the observations through a sensor operator \(\mathcal{H}\) with noise \(\varepsilon\), and \(u_w\) the network with weights \(w\).

Reference papers

The maintainer's reference papers on nonlinear uncertainty (the Oviedo particle-swarm work on sampling equivalence regions) are summarized in Equivalence regions and swarm sampling and cited by DOI. The PDFs stay out of the repository.

docs.title: The loss is a negative log-posterior
docs.text:
Take Gaussian observation noise, \(y_i = (\mathcal{H}u)_i + \varepsilon_i\) with \(\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_i^2)\), and a Gaussian belief that the residual, the boundary and the initial mismatch are zero with scales \(\sigma_r\), \(\sigma_b\), \(\sigma_0\). Up to a constant, minus the log of the posterior over \((w, \theta)\) is

\[ -\log p(w, \theta \mid y) = \frac{1}{2\sigma_r^2}\|\mathcal{N}_\theta[u_w]\|^2 + \frac{1}{2\sigma_b^2}\|\mathcal{B}u_w\|^2 + \frac{1}{2\sigma_0^2}\|u_w(\cdot, 0) - u_0\|^2 + \sum_i \frac{(y_i - (\mathcal{H}u_w)_i)^2}{2\sigma_i^2} - \log p(w, \theta). \]

This is the PINN loss, with weights \(1/\sigma^2\) (Kaipio & Somersalo, 2005; Stuart, 2010). Training finds the maximum-a-posteriori point, and the weights are not tuning knobs: the data weight is the inverse noise variance, and the physics weights encode how much model error one admits. Experiment K39 tests whether setting the data weight from the measured noise beats tuned weights, which F01 motivates: a fixed weight that ignores the noise level biased the estimate at few, noisy points.

Two things follow for pinnrl. A per-sensor noise level is a per-observation weight, which fisher_information already accepts. And a change of weights is a change of prior, so results obtained with different weights are not comparable without saying so.

docs.title: Sources of uncertainty
docs.text:
An error bar on \(\theta\) must say which of these it covers.

Source Where it comes from How it shows Aleatoric measurement noise \(\varepsilon\) the spread across noise draws; bounded below by \(F^{-1}\) Parametric epistemic finite data, correlated parameters the posterior width along sloppy directions Surrogate the network's approximation error and the non-convex training the bias of F01, the seed spread Model form the equation is not the process a residual structure the surrogate cannot remove (F08)

The Fisher bound covers the first. Ensembles over seeds and over noise draws separate the first from the third. Model-form error is the one that no method internal to the model detects, and it is why a twin must report its residual against the plant.

docs.title: Approximating the posterior
docs.text:
• Laplace. Expand the loss to second order at the optimum; the posterior is Gaussian with covariance the inverse Hessian (MacKay, 1992). The block for \(\theta\), after eliminating \(w\), is the generalized Gauss–Newton approximation of \(F^{-1}\). It reuses the sensitivities of identifiability, which is why the conditioning module comes first on the roadmap. Experiment K41 asks how much of the network the Hessian must cover.
  • Deep ensembles. Retrain from several initializations and treat the estimates as posterior samples (Lakshminarayanan, Pritzel & Blundell, 2017). The spread captures the surrogate's non-convexity, which Laplace does not, and misses nothing that retraining reveals. Experiments F06 and K40 measure coverage against the ensemble size.
  • Sampling. Hamiltonian Monte Carlo over \((w, \theta)\) (Yang, Meng & Karniadakis, 2021) is the reference posterior for small networks (K42) and too costly for the rest.
  • Conformal intervals. Hold out sensors, calibrate the residual quantile on them, and get finite-sample coverage with no distributional assumption (Vovk, Gammerman & Shafer, 2005). It bounds the field prediction rather than \(\theta\) (K44).

A broad comparison of these on physics-informed models is Psaros et al. (2023).

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
An interval is calibrated when it contains the truth as often as it claims: a 90 % interval, over many data sets, should cover 90 % of the time. Coverage alone is not enough, since an interval that is always the whole real line is calibrated. The quantities pinnrl reports, from F06 and K10 onward, are:

  • empirical coverage of the nominal interval across synthetic data sets with known truth;
  • width, the sharpness, which should be as small as coverage allows (Gneiting, Balabdaoui & Raftery, 2007);
  • the continuous ranked probability score, a proper scoring rule that rewards both at once (Gneiting & Raftery, 2007).

A method is kept only where it is calibrated, and the page of each method states the regime in which that was checked.
